title: Venus-grade NEMS relay access gives charge node zero off-current
idea: Designed for 460C Venus landers where any junction leaks, the access transistor is replaced by a SiC/TiN nanoelectromechanical contact relay whose open vacuum gap passes literally zero current. The storage node becomes a small MIM or the gate of a read transistor and holds charge for hours to days at room temperature.
why: Removes the access-transistor leakage tail (fact 3), so refresh energy (~46 fJ/bit, 16-33% of idle power) and the refresh bandwidth tax go to ~0; also hot and rad-hard. Contact endurance (~1e10-1e12 shown) must be pushed toward 1e15 with low-force contacts.

title: Liquid-nitrogen memory pods shrink the capacitor to planar 1 fF
idea: Borrowing from 77 K cryo-computing users, DRAM dies run immersed in LN2 where trap-assisted and subthreshold leakage fall ~1e6x and sense-amp offsets shrink, so retention reaches minutes. The 60:1 pillar is replaced by a ~1-1.5 fF planar or shallow-cup MIM read on short 64-cell bitlines.
why: Attacks the capacitor charge wall (fact 1) and refresh (fact 3): HAR etch/deposition steps disappear (~30-50% capacitor-module cost) and refresh power goes to ~0; the ~10 W/W cryocooler overhead must be amortized at rack scale.

title: Quantum-paraelectric strontium titanate capacitor with k near ten thousand
idea: Cryogenic quantum-computer controllers can use SrTiO3, whose permittivity climbs to ~1e4 near 4 K because quantum fluctuations suppress ferroelectric order, giving tens of fF in a planar 0.01 um2 cell. The generalizable version strain-tunes SrTiO3/KTaO3 superlattices on scandate-like buffers so the incipient-ferroelectric permittivity peak sits at 300-350 K, targeting k~300-1000.
why: Beats the k~70 requirement of fact 1 by 5-100x so the 60-75:1 pillar collapses to a planar stack; dead-layer and leakage control in sub-10 nm films is the hard part.

title: Write-once-per-session charge-trap cells for append-only AI KV caches
idea: KV caches are appended once per token, read thousands of times and discarded at session end, so each location sees ~1e4-1e6 writes per lifetime, not 1e15. Bits are electrons in a thin SiN/Al2O3 trap layer programmed by 50-100 ns channel-hot-electron pulses, bulk-erased per page at session end and read non-destructively by threshold sensing.
why: Charge-trap cells are 4F2 and 3D-stackable with no capacitor (facts 1-2), no refresh and non-destructive read (fact 8): ~5-10x density vs DRAM for this extreme workload, with endurance demand matched by write rarity.

title: Error-tolerant AI cells with half-height capacitors and BER budget
idea: LLM weights and activations survive ~1e-5 bit error rates in low-order mantissa bits, so an 'approximate' DRAM grade uses 2-2.5 fF capacitors at AR ~30:1 with longer refresh, while sign and exponent bits live in a few full-charge rows of the same mat. The storage element is deliberately under-built where the extreme user does not care.
why: Halves capacitor aspect ratio (fact 1), cutting HAR etch/deposition cost and refresh power ~2x for the ~70% of AI bits that tolerate noise: roughly 15-25% cost-per-bit gain.

title: Vacuum-gap floating electrode written by Fowler-Nordheim tunneling, oxide-free
idea: For reactor and deep-space users whose oxides trap radiation charge and wear out, the storage node is a metal island over a sealed 2-3 nm vacuum gap; electrons are written and erased by field emission through vacuum and the island gates a read transistor. Vacuum has no bonds to break or traps to fill, so tunnel wear disappears.
why: A flash-like non-volatile, non-destructive-read cell with DRAM-class endurance: no refresh (fact 3), no capacitor (fact 1), ~10-100 ns writes at 3-5 V; gap uniformity at the angstrom level is the risk.

title: Radiation-proof snap-through buckled nanobeam holds bit mechanically
idea: Satellite memory must ignore single-event upsets, so a 200 nm compressively pre-stressed SiN or TiN beam is buckled up or down; an electrostatic pulse snaps it between the two stable shapes in ~5-20 ns and a capacitive readout senses its position. There is no stored charge for a heavy ion to disturb and standby power is zero.
why: Non-volatile, rad-immune, BEOL-compatible bit with no capacitor wall (fact 1) and no refresh (fact 3); nanobeam endurance beyond 1e12 cycles and stiction are risks, density ~10-20F2 initially.

title: Polarization-bound GaN quantum-well charge storage for 200C downhole tools
idea: Oil-well logging tools need memory at 200C; an AlN/GaN/AlN double heterostructure forms a 2DEG well bounded by 6.2 eV AlN barriers and fixed polarization charge, so an injected electron sheet barely emits thermally. The stored sheet modulates an adjacent HEMT channel for non-destructive read, built in existing U.S. 200 mm GaN-on-Si power fabs.
why: Ultra-wide barriers cut leakage >1e6x vs Si junctions, giving seconds-to-hours room-temperature retention (fact 3) without a capacitor (fact 1), on U.S.-available GaN capacity (manufacturability).

title: Field-immune antiferromagnetic Neel-vector bit for EMP-hardened military memory
idea: EMP-hardened systems need storage unaffected by external fields, so the bit is the Neel vector of a noncollinear antiferromagnet such as Mn3Sn, switched by spin-orbit torque in ~10-100 ps and read through its anomalous Hall or tunnel magnetoresistance. Zero stray field lets cells pack at minimum pitch without dipolar crosstalk.
why: Unlimited endurance, non-volatile, picosecond writes potentially below DRAM CV2 energy (fact 10); removes refresh entirely; small readout signal is the main risk.

title: Piezo-strain switched pressure-sensitive phase bit from deep-sea electronics
idea: Deep-sea designers see pressure shift material phases; on chip, a thin piezoelectric (PMN-PT or AlScN) squeezes a pressure-sensitive layer such as SmSe or a Mott oxide by GPa-equivalent stress, switching its resistance 100-1000x, while a ferroelastic latch in the piezo holds the strain. Writing needs ~100-200 mV because strain, not current, does the work.
why: Breaks the voltage floor (fact 10): write energy ~1 fJ/bit vs tens of fJ, non-volatile and refresh-free; nanoscale strain transfer and fatigue are risks.

title: Tunnel-diode latched storage node for always-on phone sensor hubs
idea: Phones' always-on hubs burn standby power on refresh, so two series interband tunnel diodes (Si/SiGe Esaki) form a Goto pair on each storage node, creating two stable voltages held by picoamp valley currents. The access transistor reads and writes as usual; the node simply never decays.
why: Eliminates refresh (fact 3, 16-33% idle power) with ~pA/cell standby at near-1T1C area; requires tight peak/valley current control in BEOL-compatible tunnel diodes.

title: Negative-capacitance ferroelectric layer boosts storage capacitance for 0.5-V hearing aids
idea: Hearing aids run from ~1 V cells and want sub-0.5 V arrays; a stabilized negative-capacitance HZO layer in series with a ZrO2 positive capacitor makes the stack's effective capacitance exceed either layer alone, behaving like k~100-200. The extra charge keeps the same sense signal at half the array voltage.
why: Attacks the charge wall (fact 1) and CV2 voltage floor (fact 10): ~2-4x lower energy per bit if NC stays hysteresis-free at ns speed, a contested claim.

title: Multi-electron redox molecules as pseudocapacitive storage for printed sensors
idea: Disposable printed sensors need cheap memory, so the storage electrode carries a self-assembled monolayer of porphyrin/ferrocene multi-redox molecules that each hold 2-4 electrons at distinct potentials, giving 5-10x the charge per area of a dielectric capacitor. Charging through short molecular tethers takes tens of ns and the distinct redox levels allow 2 bits per cell.
why: Faradaic pseudocapacitance beats the dielectric charge wall (fact 1) without high aspect ratio and adds multi-level storage; molecular stability over 1e15 cycles is the risk.

title: Four-level analog charge storage borrowed from particle-detector pipelines
idea: Collider front-ends store analog samples on capacitors at 40 MHz; applied to DRAM, each cell holds one of four voltage levels, sensed by a two-step successive-approximation sense amplifier, with a per-row reference cell written alongside the data to track leakage drift. Two bits live in one capacitor.
why: 2x bits per capacitor (density, ~40% lower cost per bit) on existing cells; needs ~3x tighter signal margins and faster refresh, so it pairs with larger-Cs or lower-leakage cells.

title: Charge-coupled serial memory tier for streaming camera frame buffers
idea: Edge cameras write and read frames sequentially, so bits are stored as charge packets in a CCD-style buried channel and clocked along gates with no per-bit access transistor or contact; random access happens at block granularity through a small SRAM head. Each bit occupies ~2-3F2 with no capacitor pillar.
why: Removes the access transistor, contacts and capacitor (facts 1-3) and most periphery (fact 7): 2-3x density for sequential tiers such as frame buffers or streamed KV caches; transfer efficiency and latency are the trade.

title: Mixed-conductor volumetric capacitance storage node from wearable bioelectronics
idea: Wearable sensors use organic mixed ionic-electronic conductors such as PEDOT:PSS whose entire volume charges at ~40 F/cm3, so a 100 nm cube stores ~40 fF, ~8x a DRAM pillar. A sealed solid-electrolyte version (polymerized ionic liquid) aims for 10-100 ns charging because ion diffusion time shrinks with the square of size.
why: Destroys the capacitor charge wall (fact 1) with no high aspect ratio and leaves room for multi-level storage; ion speed and 1e15-cycle stability are unproven.

title: Self-healing ferroelectric nematic liquid in nano-wells, fatigue-free
idea: Thirty-year industrial controllers cannot tolerate ferroelectric fatigue, so polarization is held by a ferroelectric nematic liquid crystal (P ~4-6 uC/cm2) sealed in nano-wells; being a fluid, pinned domains and defects anneal away, removing wake-up and fatigue. Surface anchoring gives two stable polar orientations, read by displacement charge or a coupled FET.
why: Promises effectively unlimited polarization endurance with ~5x the charge per area of a DRAM capacitor; switching (us today) must reach ~100 ns through nanoscale confinement.

title: Picosecond-switched hidden charge-density-wave state in 1T-TaS2 bits
idea: Cryogenic and ultrafast computing users exploit 1T-TaS2's metastable 'hidden' charge-density-wave state, entered by a ~30 ps electrical pulse and exited by a longer heating pulse, with 10-100x resistance contrast. Strain or doping engineering pushes the hidden state's lifetime from cryogenic toward room temperature for DRAM-like retention.
why: fJ-class picosecond switching (facts 5, 10) in a 2D layer stackable in BEOL; room-temperature retention is the speculative step.

title: Nanobattery voltage-mode bit read potentiometrically, signal independent of size
idea: EV battery managers read cell voltage, not charge; likewise each bit is a solid-state micro-battery (LixTiO2/LiPON-like stack) whose open-circuit voltage differs by ~0.3 V between states, sensed by a high-impedance FET gate. A battery's voltage does not shrink with its area, so the read signal survives scaling where capacitor charge does not.
why: Sidesteps the capacitor charge wall entirely (fact 1); quasi-non-volatile with no refresh; ion kinetics (us) and cycle life are the obstacles.

title: Photonic-crystal nanocavity bistable bits for optical router packet buffers
idea: Optical packet routers want buffers that stay in the optical domain; InP or Si photonic-crystal nanocavities with carrier-induced bistability hold a bit at ~30-100 nW while light circulates and switch with fJ optical pulses. Placed beside co-packaged optics they cache data in flight without O-E-O conversion.
why: Targets data-movement energy (fact 5) in interconnect-heavy AI fabrics; density is low (~um2/bit), so it is a small fast tier, not bulk DRAM.

title: Few-electron storage read by single-electron transistor for smart dust
idea: Millimeter smart-dust nodes cannot afford 30,000-electron capacitors, so a 5-10 nm Si island stores ~50-200 electrons and an adjacent room-temperature single-electron transistor converts each added electron into a large current swing. The storage element shrinks to aF-scale capacitance with no pillar.
why: Removes the charge wall (fact 1) and cuts write energy ~100x (fact 10); room-temperature SET variability and background offset charges are the barrier.

title: VO2 thermal-hysteresis bit held at hot-water-cooled datacenter temperature
idea: Hot-water-cooled racks run silicon at ~60-65C, inside VO2's insulator-metal hysteresis loop; at that bias temperature a nano-island is bistable, set metallic by a short Joule pulse and reset by a field or cooling pulse, and read by its 100-1000x resistance contrast. The extreme cooling regime itself becomes the storage mechanism.
why: Zero-standby, refresh-free bit with ns switching (fact 3); nanoscale hysteresis width and thermal crosstalk between neighbors are the risks.

title: Pulsed-power antiferroelectric charge release triples DRAM read signal
idea: Pulsed-power capacitors use antiferroelectrics because field-induced polarization dumps large charge on discharge; a ZrO2-rich antiferroelectric capacitor written to '1' sits in the field-induced polar state and, during charge sharing, back-switches to release ~3-5x the charge of a linear dielectric, while a '0' releases only linear charge. No remanence is used, so fatigue stays modest.
why: Effective k ~100+ during read (fact 1) lets the pillar drop from 70:1 to ~25:1; the '1' level must exceed the ~1.5 MV/cm forward switching field, partly fighting the voltage floor (fact 10).

title: Single-implant gated-diode amplifying cell for $1 IoT microcontrollers
idea: A $1 IoT MCU in 40 nm logic needs megabytes of RAM without a capacitor module; one added implant mask forms a gated diode whose gate capacitance is large when '1' is stored (inverted) and tiny when '0', so boosting the gate during read amplifies the '1' several-fold (2T1D cell). Everything else uses existing logic layers.
why: ~3x denser-than-SRAM embedded working memory for one mask, cutting MCU die cost; the self-amplifying node needs ~5x less Cs (fact 1).

title: FD-SOI back-plane island stores bit beneath buried oxide
idea: Space-grade FD-SOI already sits on a thin buried oxide; one implant mask forms isolated doped islands in the handle wafer under each transistor, and charge injected into an island shifts the front channel threshold through the 20 nm BOX like a back gate. The BOX shields the island from front-side transient strikes and front junction leakage.
why: Capacitorless gain-type cell at ~4-6F2 with ~10x the retention of floating-body cells (facts 1, 3), on existing FD-SOI lines including U.S. capacity, for one mask.

title: Diffusion-barrier monolayer at storage-node contact for 200C retention
idea: Downhole tools at 200C expose tail cells whose mid-gap traps come from contact-metal atoms diffusing into the storage junction; an ALD AlN or hBN monolayer is deposited blanket into the existing storage-node contact holes as a diffusion barrier, and the single added mask only strips it from periphery contacts. The storage junction stays defect-free so its generation current collapses.
why: Trims the leakage tail (fact 3) by ~10x, stretching refresh interval and saving 10-20% of idle power; added contact resistance must stay below ~10 kohm.

title: Deep-level dopant pocket memory from cryogenic dopant freeze-out
idea: Quantum-computer controllers at 4-40 K watch shallow dopants freeze out and hold their charge state for hours; the room-temperature analog implants, with one mask, a pocket of deep-level dopants (S, Se or Zn in Si, 0.3-0.6 eV) under the access device so captured electrons take milliseconds to minutes to re-emit. Pocket occupancy shifts the device threshold as the stored bit.
why: Capacitorless storage governed by emission-time physics rather than leakage paths (facts 1, 3); one implant mask; capture speed and uniform trap density are the risks.

title: MOS-varactor storage node read nondestructively by RF capacitance sensing
idea: KV caches read each bit thousands of times, so one added implant mask converts the storage node into a depletion-type MOS varactor whose capacitance depends on its stored voltage; a small high-frequency probe on the plate senses that capacitance via the bitline without draining charge. Writes stay conventional; reads stop being destructive.
why: Kills destructive read and restore energy (fact 8, ~5.9 pJ per useful bit) and the activations that drive row hammer (fact 9); detecting small capacitance changes on long bitlines is the risk.

title: Work-function-offset antiferroelectric gives two zero-bias states for pacemakers
idea: Pacemakers need memory that idles at zero power for ten years; one added mask patterns a high-work-function RuO2 top electrode (vs TiN) over ZrO2-rich antiferroelectric capacitors, shifting one double-hysteresis loop so two polarization states coexist at 0 V. Antiferroelectric switching avoids HZO wake-up and offers 1e12+ endurance.
why: Non-volatile, refresh-free capacitor in the existing cell geometry for one mask (fact 3); read remains destructive but refresh energy and standby power vanish.

title: Mask-selected ferroelectric phase makes hybrid volatile and persistent mats
idea: Industrial controllers want working memory that snapshots on power loss; a thin Si- or La-oxide dopant sublayer is deposited blanket before the ZrO2 dielectric and the single added mask strips it from ordinary mats, so on anneal the doped mats crystallize orthorhombic (ferroelectric) and the rest tetragonal (linear high-k). One die carries DRAM mats and persistent ferroelectric mats from one flow.
why: Puts non-volatile snapshot capacity on the DRAM die, removing separate backup memory and enabling instant-on; uniform dopant coverage in 60:1 pillars is the challenge.

title: Single cut-mask splits each pillar into differential twin half-capacitors
idea: Avionics users fear neutron upsets; one added cut mask slices each cylindrical bottom electrode into two half-shells, each on its own access path, storing complementary charges. Reading the pair differentially doubles signal per stored charge, removes reference cells and half-VDD bitline noise, and a strike on one half cannot flip the comparison alone.
why: 2x effective sense margin per electron allows ~0.7 V arrays (fact 10) or shorter pillars (fact 1); costs one cut mask and a second access device per pillar.

title: Dual-bit cell stores capacitor charge and floating-body charge together
idea: Million-token AI contexts are capacity-starved, so one counter-doping implant mask isolates a floating p-pocket under each access transistor; the cell keeps one bit as capacitor charge and a second as body holes that shift threshold. Reads first sense the body bit by current at an intermediate wordline level, then charge-share the capacitor bit.
why: Up to 2x bits per cell area on existing 6F2 arrays for one mask (density, cost per bit); body/capacitor disturb coupling and two retention clocks are the risks.

title: Stacked antiferroelectric staircase capacitor stores three charge levels
idea: Downlink-limited imaging satellites value capacity per gram; the capacitor dielectric becomes a bilayer of two antiferroelectric films with different switching fields (ZrO2 and Hf-doped ZrO2), yielding a staircase charge-voltage curve with three flat plateaus, so each cell holds 1.58 bits with wide margins. The only added mask restores the old dielectric for periphery decoupling capacitors.
why: ~1.5x bits per pillar (density, cost per bit); plateaus give better multi-level margins than linear analog levels.

title: Silicon-on-nothing vacuum-isolated membrane holds charge at 300C
idea: For hot users such as Venus probes and jet-engine controllers, one trench-array mask followed by a hydrogen anneal migrates silicon to seal an empty cavity under a thin Si membrane (empty-space-in-silicon process); the membrane is the storage body, isolated below by vacuum instead of junctions. Charge in the membrane modulates the overlying channel.
why: Removes the substrate-junction leakage component (fact 3) for 10-100x retention in a capacitorless cell (fact 1); one mask; membrane thickness uniformity is the risk.

title: Single reticle exposed twice rotated forms OTS-selected cross-point capacitors
idea: Hyperscale AI wants density but allows one new mask, so a lines-and-spaces reticle is exposed once for rows and again rotated 90 degrees for columns, patterning a BEOL cross-point of ovonic-threshold-switch plus MIM capacitor stacks at 4F2. The switch's steep sub-threshold cut-off isolates each capacitor, and further decks reuse the same reticle.
why: Stackable 4F2 BEOL DRAM tiers (facts 2, 4) with no new transistors and one reticle; OTS leakage at half-select bias sets retention to us-ms, the key physics risk.

title: Fatigue-free sliding ferroelectric bilayer for fifty-year deep-space probes
idea: Voyager-class probes need 50-year memory; MOCVD-grown bilayer MoS2 or hBN shows 'sliding' ferroelectricity in which polarization flips by a lateral interlayer shift without breaking bonds and shows no measurable fatigue. One mask patterns the BEOL bilayer into capacitors or FeFET gates over existing vias.
why: Atomically thin polarization storage with potentially unlimited endurance and sub-1 V switching (fact 10); wafer-scale control of bilayer stacking order is the risk.

title: One hole mask defines every tier's annular capacitor in 3D
idea: Exascale machines need TB-class capacity; borrowing 3D NAND punch-and-plug, a single deep-hole mask through a 48-tier Si/SiGe stack is followed by lateral recess etches that carve an annular storage node and gate in every tier self-aligned to the hole, all tied to a shared vertical bitline.
why: Beats fact 2's 26+ tier break-even with only one critical mask for all tiers, collapsing litho cost per bit (fact 4); recess-etch uniformity across 48 tiers is the risk.

title: Segmented plate-line bootstraps stored charge for 0.4 V harvesters
idea: Thermoelectric-harvesting IoT runs at ~0.4 V; one cut mask splits the common capacitor plate into per-row plate lines so the selected row's plate is pulsed during read, bootstrapping the stored node ~2x before charge sharing. The bit is written at low array voltage yet read with a full-size signal.
why: Breaks the ~1 V VARY floor (fact 10) for ~4x lower CV2 write energy with one mask; plate-line drivers add periphery area (fact 7).

title: Self-gated keeper turns charge cell static for polar-night weather stations
idea: Arctic stations sleep for months on stored energy; one implant mask forms a tiny vertical keeper transistor along each storage-node sidewall, gated by the node itself and fed from a VDD-biased diffusion shared by neighbors, so a '1' weakly turns on its keeper and tops itself up while a '0' stays off. Leakage-ratio bistability, as in loadless 4T SRAM, replaces refresh.
why: Refresh-free (fact 3) at near-1T1C area for one mask; keeper current must beat the ~13 fA leakage tail yet stay at pA level.

title: Phase-state NEMS parametron for megagray nuclear reactor instrumentation
idea: Reactor instruments absorb megagray doses that wreck oxides and stored charge, so bits are stored as the oscillation phase (0 or pi) of parametrically pumped nanobeams, as in 1950s parametron computers; one release mask lets a vapor etch free beams from an existing BEOL metal layer. A shared pump keeps beams oscillating and reads detect phase capacitively.
why: Radiation-immune, refresh-free while pumped and wear-free; low density (~um2/bit) makes it a niche tier, but it proves charge-free storage in BEOL for one mask.

title: Photodiode storage node written by co-packaged laser light
idea: Laser-crosslink satellites receive data as light, so one implant mask turns storage nodes into Si photodiode junctions under a transparent plate; rows are precharged to '1' and a modulated micro-LED/VCSEL array discharges the '0' cells optically in parallel, while reads stay electrical. Write drivers and write bitline swings largely disappear.
why: Cuts write data-movement energy (fact 5) and periphery (fact 7) for streaming-write workloads; optical alignment and neighbor crosstalk are the risks.

title: Self-clearing segmented electrode capacitor from subsea repeater film capacitors
idea: Subsea repeaters rely on metallized-film capacitors that vaporize their thin electrode around a breakdown spot and keep working; one mask patterns a 3-5 nm top-electrode film into fusible micro-segments so a dielectric breakdown burns out only its local segment. Tolerating breakdown lets the dielectric thin by ~30%.
why: ~1.3-1.4x capacitance with no new material (fact 1) and higher yield because breakdown no longer kills a cell; nanoscale fuse energetics are the risk.

title: Dipolar molecular rotors in nanogaps store dynamic bits for ingestible pills
idea: Ingestible sensor pills need tiny, low-voltage memory; one mask opens nanogaps where a self-assembled monolayer of dipolar molecular rotors aligns up or down under ~0.3 V, and the collective dipole shifts a sense FET threshold. Thermal relaxation over milliseconds makes it a natural refreshed dynamic bit with no bond-breaking wear.
why: Sub-0.5 V writes (fact 10) and no capacitor wall (fact 1); retention vs density and rotor uniformity are speculative.

title: Conductive ferroelectric domain walls repurpose U.S. lithium niobate photonics fabs
idea: Telecom photonics users already run thin-film lithium niobate lines; one mask adds electrode pairs on LNOI so writing a domain creates a charged, conductive domain wall between them, read non-destructively by its 1e3-1e5 current contrast without switching polarization.
why: Non-destructive read (fact 8), non-volatile, ns writes on existing U.S. photonics capacity (manufacturability); domain-wall reliability below 50 nm is the risk.

title: Self-ordered anodic alumina nanopores multiply capacitor area for embargoed fabs
idea: A fab cut off from EUV, tungsten and helium can still anodize aluminum: one mask defines array regions in a BEOL Al layer that anodizes into self-ordered 20-30 nm pores at >100:1 aspect ratio, which are ALD-coated with TiN/ZrO2/TiN to form massive storage capacitors above the transistors. Self-assembly replaces HAR plasma etch and EUV patterning.
why: >=10 fF per cell without HAR etch tools (facts 1, 4) using abundant Al (scarce-resource intensity, U.S. manufacturability); registering pores to cells is the risk.

title: Radar pulse-forming inspired internal-barrier nanolaminate with giant permittivity
idea: Radar pulse-forming networks prize giant-permittivity dielectrics; a nanolaminate of 0.5 nm insulating Al2O3 barriers between 2 nm semiconducting TiO2-x layers shows Maxwell-Wagner giant effective k (~1000), deposited blanket into pillars with one mask protecting periphery. Tuning sublayer conductivity pushes the relaxation frequency above ~1 GHz so the high k survives ns charge sharing.
why: k_eff 10x+ over ZrO2 (fact 1) could cut pillars to AR ~10:1; leakage vs relaxation speed is a fundamental trade, hence speculative.
